examples.label: SAM/SYSTEM backups often left in repair
IIS web app config with connection strings

notes:
=== Files of Interest Reference — Extended Credential and Sensitive Data Locations ===
Comprehensive checklist of high-value file locations to check during post-exploitation.

=== HIGH-VALUE REGISTRY HIVE COPIES ===
C:\Windows\repair\SAM              → backup SAM hive (local account hashes)
C:\Windows\repair\SYSTEM           → needed to decrypt SAM
C:\Windows\system32\config\SAM    → live (locked) - access via VSS or SeBackupPrivilege
C:\Windows\system32\config\SYSTEM → live (locked) - same
C:\Windows\system32\config\*.sav  → .sav extension = backup copies from Windows Setup

=== LOG AND CONFIG FILES ===
%WINDIR%\System32\CCM\logs\*.log          → SCCM deployment logs (may contain credentials)
%WINDIR%\System32\drivers\etc\hosts       → internal DNS names / network topology
C:\inetpub\wwwroot\web.config             → IIS connection strings
C:\inetpub\wwwroot\*\appsettings.json    → .NET Core connection strings
*.rdp files anywhere                         → saved RDP sessions with encoded credentials
*.vnc files                                  → VNC password configuration
*.config files                               → application configuration
NetSetup.log                                 → domain join credentials

=== VIRTUAL DISK AND BACKUP FILES ===
*.vhd, *.vhdx files               → Hyper-V virtual disk images (mount offline for full OS access)
*.vmdk files                      → VMware virtual disk images
*.bak, *.backup files             → application database backups (may contain credentials)
SQL database backup files (.bak)  → may restore to extract credentials from app DB

=== MEMORY AND PAGE FILES ===
C:\pagefile.sys                   → system page file (may contain memory-resident credentials)
C:\hiberfil.sys                   → hibernation file (full memory snapshot — contains credentials)
%temp%\*.dmp                      → crash dumps (may contain LSASS memory)

=== SNAFFLER FOR AUTOMATED SWEEP ===
.\Snaffler.exe -s -d <domain> -o snaffler.log -v data
Snaffler specifically targets file extensions and content patterns known to contain credentials
Searches network shares — finds web.config, connection strings, password files, SSH keys

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
.sav registry files → secretsdump offline → local account hashes without admin tools
Virtual disk files on backup shares → mount offline → full OS credential access
hiberfil.sys → volatility/strings extraction → memory-resident credentials
pagefile.sys analysis → find credentials that were swapped to disk
SCCM logs → deployment account credentials → lateral movement across managed systems

recommended.note: Seize ownership to read these when locked.
